one_line: A huge two-handed ram that a player can equip, wind up, and swing to demolish airlocks and knock people over, insulating the wielder from airlock shocks while held.
player_facing_mechanics: Pick up and carry/wield a huge two-handed item (back slot, slows movement and dragging while held)
Swing requires a two-hand wield and a wind-up animation/sound before each strike, interruptible
Deals high brute damage (20 wielded, 5 unwielded) with extra wound bonus and strong structure/airlock demolition (demolition_mod 3, ~9 hits per airlock)
Wielding it grants immunity to airlock shocks; dropping it removes that immunity
Hitting a standing, unanchored mob throws them one tile; in zero gravity the user is thrown back instead
Hitting with it costs the user stamina loss (9) each swing
Attacking an open door knocks the user down and throws them into it with a message
Clumsy users have a 30% chance to slip and be knocked down when swinging
Nearby bystanders within 2 tiles get a camera shake on impact
Throwing it deals 14 throwforce over a range of 2
Suicide action (BRUTELOSS) with a custom verb-based message

demolition_mod, wound_bonus, bare_wound_bonus, throwforce, slowdown, drag_slowdown, throw_range

port_notes: This is a single self-contained melee item and maps cleanly: an ItemComponent with MeleeWeapon/DamageOtherOnHit stats, a TwoHanded/HandHeldComponent equivalent, a WieldableComponent, and an ItemToggle or actions system for the wind-up. The equip/drop signal handlers become a component that subscribes to equipment events and applies/removes an immunity status effect or mob trait (shock immunity), and the wind-up becomes a DoAfter with its own cancellation event. The quirky physics (throw-on-hit, zero-g recoil, clumsy self-throw) and the open-door knockdown need a human to decide whether they belong in a dedicated BatteringRamSystem or in generic melee/projectile-throw systems; the referenced /obj/structure/fireaxecabinet/batteringram variant is not defined in this file and must be sourced separately. Balance values (demolition_mod, wound bonus, slowdown, stamina cost) are pure data and belong in YAML prototypes.
